findings.description: The RDS instance sets publicly_accessible = true, giving it a public endpoint reachable from the internet rather than being confined to the VPC. Combined with an internet-exposed MySQL listener this greatly expands attack surface for a data store.
storage_encrypted = false disables KMS encryption of the RDS storage volume and snapshots, leaving database contents unprotected at rest.

The master username is hardcoded as 'admin' and the password is supplied through a plain Terraform variable, which is stored in cleartext in Terraform state and is also interpolated into EC2 user data elsewhere in this file, rather than being sourced from Secrets Manager.
No parameter or option enforces TLS for client connections (e.g. require_secure_transport), so the application connects over plaintext MySQL and credentials/data can be intercepted.
The MySQL parameter group does not set require_secure_transport = 1, so unencrypted client connections to the database are permitted.

The EC2 user_data script embeds the database username and password (var.password) in cleartext into dbinfo.inc. User data is retrievable from the instance metadata service by any process or SSRF vulnerability on the host and is stored unencrypted in the instance configuration.
No root_block_device/ebs encryption is configured for the instance, so the volume holding the credential file /var/www/inc/dbinfo.inc may be stored unencrypted at rest.

No metadata_options block requiring http_tokens = "required" is set, leaving IMDSv1 enabled. Because the instance runs an internet-facing PHP application with a highly privileged instance profile, an SSRF flaw could be used to steal role credentials.
The bootstrap script installs and serves the application over plain HTTP (httpd with no TLS), so form submissions containing employee data traverse the network in cleartext.

The inline role policy grants s3:*, ec2:* and rds:* on Resource "*", violating least privilege. This role is attached to an internet-facing EC2 instance, so compromise of the web app yields near-total control of S3, EC2 and RDS, including privilege escalation via instance/role manipulation.

Egress on all protocols and ports to 0.0.0.0/0 from the database security group permits unrestricted outbound traffic, enabling data exfiltration or command-and-control from a compromised database host.

findings.issue_category: missing rule descriptions and implicit trust
findings.description: The RDS security group has no description on its rules and permits MySQL from the entire VPC CIDR rather than only the application instance's security group, granting any workload in the VPC direct database access.
